summary: Feed s110_single is degraded: 20.4% of TCP sessions (23/113) are one-way, exceeding 10% threshold for IDS that requires bidirectional traffic. All other checks (duplicates, encrypted share, VLAN 10/20, packet drops, tool overload) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or TAP/SPAN aggregation is not delivering both directions of the same session to the IDS tool port. 20.4% one-way indicates asymmetric forwarding - likely only client-to-server or server-to-client is being forwarded, or east/west paths are split across different broker ingress ports without aggregation.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_both_directions=true for stateful TCP reassembly and signature matching. One-way sessions prevent stream reconstruction, causing missed detections, incomplete flows, and high false-negative rate for exploits and C2.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow to the same IDS tool port on the packet broker to restore full bidirectional visibility required for stateful inspection.
